title: Research Grok Bot conversation storage
description:
Research where the Grok Bot desktop AI assistant app stores conversations on macOS: app container paths, database or file formats, session and authorship semantics, timestamps, and any dedup or fork behavior. Cite public docs or source where they exist; mark anything unverifiable as an assumption to check against a real Mac with the app installed. Nothing is assumed from the other adapters — Grok Bot gets its own research pass.

Done when: a research summary with citations or clearly marked assumptions is recorded on this issue and validated against a real Mac.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: BLOCKED on real-Mac research — cannot be done from this VM (no macOS, no Grok Bot install). What to research on Ryan's Mac with Grok Bot installed: (1) storage location — look under ~/Library/Containers/<bundle-id>/ and ~/Library/Application Support/ for the app's data dir; (2) format — SQLite (file magic 'SQLite format 3', then .tables/.schema) vs JSON/JSONL, and where conversation/message rows or files live; (3) session semantics — how one conversation is identified, whether there are folders/projects to attribute to; (4) authorship — which field reliably distinguishes human messages from assistant or injected (system prompt, tool, notification) content; (5) timestamps — epoch vs ISO, local vs UTC; (6) dedup/fork behavior — is the same message ever stored twice (e.g. retries, sync)? Record citations or mark each claim as an assumption, then validate against the real install. Once recorded, a1a9d4 (fixture capture) follows.
